pharm: Potent dopamine D2 receptor antagonist used to suppress motor and phonic tics in Tourette's disorder; prolongs the QT interval.
quick: Start 1-2 mg/day divided; maintain <0.2 mg/kg/day or 10 mg/day
With or without food; avoid grapefruit juice
Use only if clearly needed; neonatal EPS/withdrawal risk
summary: Pimozide is a typical antipsychotic indicated specifically for suppression of motor and phonic tics in Tourette's disorder in patients who have failed standard treatment. It requires slow, gradual titration with baseline and periodic ECGs because it prolongs the QT interval and has caused fatal arrhythmias. It is contraindicated with QT-prolonging drugs, CYP3A4/CYP2D6 inhibitors, in congenital long-QT syndrome, hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia, and in simple tics not due to Tourette's.
indications: Suppression of motor and phonic tics in Tourette's disorder in patients who have failed to respond satisfactorily to standard treatment

dosage.d: Start 1-2 mg/day in divided doses; increase every other day
dosage.n: Maintain at <0.2 mg/kg/day or 10 mg/day, whichever is less; max not above 0.2 mg/kg/day or 10 mg/day

dosage.d: Start 0.05 mg/kg, preferably at bedtime; increase every third day
dosage.n: Max 0.2 mg/kg/day not to exceed 10 mg/day
In poor CYP2D6 metabolizers do not exceed 4 mg/day (adults) or 0.05 mg/kg/day (children); titrate no faster than every 14 days

admin: Initiate at low dose with slow, gradual titration; balance tic suppression against adverse effects
Obtain baseline ECG and check periodically, especially during dose adjustment
Correct hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia before and during therapy
Withdraw gradually; abrupt cessation may cause transient tic worsening
moa: Potent, selective antagonist of central dopamine D2 receptors, suppressing dopaminergically mediated motor and phonic tics. It also blocks cardiac potassium channels, prolonging cardiac repolarization (QT interval).

absolute: Simple tics or tics not associated with Tourette's disorder
Concurrent drugs that themselves cause tics (pemoline, methylphenidate, amphetamines) until withdrawn
Congenital long-QT syndrome or history of cardiac arrhythmias
Concurrent strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (azole antifungals, macrolides, protease inhibitors) and CYP2D6 inhibitors (e.g., certain SSRIs)
Severe toxic CNS depression or comatose states
relative: Elderly with dementia-related psychosis (increased mortality - class effect)

preg: Use only if clearly needed. Neonates exposed in the third trimester are at risk for extrapyramidal and/or withdrawal symptoms.
lact: It is not known if pimozide is excreted in human milk but it is likely; breastfeeding is not recommended.
renal: Use with caution; no specific dosage recommendation - lower doses may be prudent.
hepatic: Use with caution and reduce dose; hepatic metabolism (CYP3A4/CYP2D6) is the main elimination route.

major: QT-prolonging drugs (class IA/III antiarrhythmics, certain antipsychotics, macrolides, fluoroquinolones, methadone) - additive QT risk, torsades
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin, erythromycin, ritonavir) - raise pimozide levels (contraindicated)
CYP2D6 inhibitors (paroxetine, fluoxetine, sertraline) - raise pimozide levels (contraindicated)
Drugs causing tics (methylphenidate, amphetamines, pemoline) - contraindicated
moderate: CNS depressants and alcohol - additive sedation
Drugs causing hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia (diuretics) - increase arrhythmia risk
interactions.food: Avoid grapefruit juice (inhibits CYP3A4 and raises pimozide levels).
interactions.diagnostics: Baseline and periodic ECG (QTc); monitor serum potassium and magnesium; consider CYP2D6 genotyping at higher doses.

serious: QT prolongation, ventricular arrhythmias including torsades de pointes, sudden death
emergency: Torsades de pointes / sudden cardiac death

monitoring: ECG (QTc) at baseline and periodically, especially during dose adjustment
Serum potassium and magnesium (correct before/during therapy)
CYP2D6 metabolizer status when exceeding threshold doses
Signs of neuroleptic malignant syndrome (fever, rigidity, autonomic instability)
counsel: Take exactly as prescribed; dose changes are made slowly
Report fainting, palpitations, or irregular heartbeat immediately (heart rhythm risk)
Report muscle stiffness, tremor, restlessness, or abnormal movements
Tell every clinician you take pimozide before starting any new medicine (many interactions)
pk: Tic suppression over days to weeks of titration
Store at room temperature, protect from light
pearls: Reserved for Tourette's tics failing standard therapy - not first-line and not for simple/non-Tourette tics
QT prolongation and torsades risk drive the contraindications - avoid QT drugs and CYP3A4/2D6 inhibitors and correct K+/Mg2+
Baseline and periodic ECG monitoring is mandatory
Long half-life means steady state and offset take days
CYP2D6 poor metabolizers need dose limits and slower titration
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered unless it is close to the next dose, then skip it; do not double up. Because of the long half-life and arrhythmia risk, do not take extra doses.
overdose: Overdose causes severe extrapyramidal reactions, hypotension, ECG changes (QT prolongation, arrhythmias), and CNS depression up to coma. There is no specific antidote; provide ECG/cardiac monitoring, supportive care, gastric decontamination, and treat arrhythmias and EPS (anticholinergics for dystonia). Avoid drugs that further prolong QT.
